newsitem.title: JORDAN: MOTOR SPORT - British jet car's first desert drive on Sunday.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR SPORT - British jet car's first desert drive on Sunday.

text.p: Britain's world land speed record challenger, the jet-powered Thrust SSC, will make its first run in the Jordanian desert shortly after dawn on November 3, a local organiser said on Monday.
Hassan Aladin said the car was being checked and tested at the military airbase where it arrived at the weekend, ahead of its first scheduled outing on the nearby Al-Jafr mudflats.
"Everything is fine, it's going to schedule," said Aladin, who is chairman of motor sports at Jordan's Royal Automobile Club, official timekeepers for the world record attempt.

Thrust project director Richard Noble, who set the existing record of 633.47 miles per hour (1,019.44 kph) in 1983, said on Saturday he was confident the 16 metre, 9.5 tonne car, powered by two jet engines from a Phantom warplane, was up to the challenge.
But he added his ultimate aim was to prepare the car for an attempt next year to break the speed of sound, which at sea level is 762 mph (1,226 kph).
Organisers say driver Andy Green will start testing the car at a sedate 200 mph (322 kph), increasing the speed by up to 100 mph (60 kph) a day.
The British team is racing to break the sound barrier ahead of long-time rival American Craig Breedlove, currently testing his car, the Spirit of America, in Nevada's Black Rock Desert.

Thrust SSC, designed to reach 850 mph (1,360 kph), is not expected to get close to that speed in Jordan because the mud flats at Jafr are just 10 miles long -- about two thirds of the distance needed for the car to reach supersonic speeds.
